title: Meta acquires AI coding start-up Conductor
summary: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor to enhance multi-agent developer tools
detailed: Meta acquired AI coding start-up Conductor, a platform allowing users to run teams of coding agents in parallel from Macs, iPhones, or the cloud.
Conductor was founded in 2024 by CEO Charlie Holtz and CTO Jackson de Campos, and raised $22 million in Series A funding in March.
While Conductor's platform will continue working normally, Conductor Cloud will shut down over the coming weeks.
The acquisition follows Conductor's July 2025 platform launch and comes amid a wave of tech acquisitions targeting developer-focused AI tools.
sentences: The platform offers users the ability to run ‘a team of coding agents’ from a Mac, iPhone or the cloud.
Meta has acquired AI coding start-up Conductor in the tech giant’s latest move to enhance its AI capabilities and offerings.

Conductor, which was founded in 2024 by CEO Charlie Holtz and CTO Jackson de Campos, offers users the ability to run “a team of coding agents” from a Mac, iPhone or the cloud, according to its website.
Its platform uses first-party agents of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode to allow developers to run multiple AI instances in parallel.
Terms of Meta’s acquisition, which was initially reported by Axios yesterday (4 November), were not disclosed.
In March, Conductor raised $22m in Series A funding from Spark and Matrix.
The start-up said its platform, launched in July 2025, “will keep working as normal” following the Meta acquisition, with the exception of Conductor Cloud shutting down over the coming weeks.
A blogpost on the deal also detailed a timeline and instructions for active and prospective users of the coding platform.
“I am very excited to share that Conductor is joining Meta,” Holtz wrote on X .

“We have some big, crazy plans for the next interface.”
Big AI companies have been keen to buy smaller businesses and platforms that offer useful AI development tools.
Yesterday, Meta rival OpenAI said it would acquire Pierre, the company behind “a family of standout open-source developer tools”.
In March, Meta acquired Moltbook , the platform for AI agents.
However, it was forced earlier this year to abandon a $2bn deal for the Chinese AI start-up Manus after intervention from China’s government blocked the acquisition for reasons of national security.
Meta’s Muse Spark Open AI model was unveiled last month.

Described as the “most capable” US open-weight model to date, the multimodal offering has 816bn total parameters, with 42bn active parameters and a 1m-token context window to assist in coding, agentic work and other complex, multi-step reasoning tasks.
